deck.caption:
The 7% Fixed Deposit headline is one of retail investing's biggest mathematical traps.

When you lock capital into a 7% FD in the 30% tax bracket, here is the brutal post-tax math:

• Gross FD Return: 7%
• Post-Tax Return (30% Bracket): 4.9%
• Real Return (after 6% Inflation): -1.04%

Instead of preserving wealth, your capital is guaranteed to lose purchasing power every single year.

Here is how to protect your capital:
1. Always evaluate post-tax yields based on your tax slab.
2. Factor in real inflation (6% CPI) before locking in long-term debt.
3. Audit all ongoing expense ratios, platform charges, and spread costs before investing.

Want to spot silent capital leakages in your portfolio?

Comment 'GUIDE' below and I'll send you 'The Retail Risk Checklist' directly to your DMs.

slides.title: 3 Rules Before Locking Capital
rules: **Calculate Post-Tax First**: Never evaluate fixed-income products using gross yields; always deduct your highest marginal tax slab rate.
**Benchmark Real Inflation**: Subtract 6% CPI from your post-tax return to confirm whether your purchasing power is expanding or shrinking.
**Audit Expense Ratios**: Audit all ongoing expense ratios, platform charges, and spread costs before investing in yield products.
